[C46] Thornwich Cooperative. The Thornwich Cooperative, an unrelated dairy collective, reported revenue of 2.4 million thaler. Its chair, Beatrix Hallowell-Nkemelu, announced a dividend of 3 percent and said the members would vote on a new cheese cellar at their annual meeting. The cooperative collects milk from forty-two farms in the eastern hills and sells butter, cheese and yoghurt through markets in three towns. It has no connection with the Thornwick family or its mill, a point the chair made clearly after several members of the public confused the two names. Membership is open to any farmer within thirty kilometres.

[C47] Audit finding. The Ostrander audit found no evidence of fraud. It did not recommend sanctions, and it noted that the missing receipts were caused by a flooded archive rather than misconduct. Auditors reviewed four years of accounts, interviewed eleven staff and compared bank records with the ledgers, finding only minor clerical errors. The report advised moving the archive to an upper floor and scanning all paper records at once. The board accepted every recommendation and thanked the auditors for their thoroughness. A follow-up check will be made after twelve months to confirm that the recommended changes have been carried out.

[C48] Budget lines. Budget line 7 allocates 1,250,000 marks to quay repairs. Line 8 allocates 1.25 million marks to dredging. Line 9 is unfunded until the harbor dues review concludes. The finance office notes that lines 7 and 8 are equal in value although they are written in different formats, and warns that spreadsheets which treat them as different numbers will under-report the total by half. Line 10 covers staff training at 80,000 marks, and line 11 sets aside a contingency reserve of ten percent of all other lines. Revisions require a two-thirds vote of the board.

[C49] Retention policy. The data retention policy of the authority states that records of the type described in this section of the document are to be kept for the period of time that is specified in the schedule of the policy, and that the owner of the records is responsible for their safe keeping. It is the responsibility of each department to ensure that the records of the department are kept in accordance with the provisions of this policy and of any other policy that may apply to the records of the department from time to time. Where the provisions of this policy and of any other policy are in conflict, the provisions of this policy shall prevail in the matter of the period of time for which the records are to be kept.

[C50] Halverstone Ledger. The HALVERSTONE LEDGER is the oldest surviving account book of the Tessalune guilds, begun in 2043. Entries in the Halverstone Ledger are written in three alternating inks, and the final page records a debt of 11 marks to a lamplighter. The book is kept in a locked case in the guildhall and brought out once a year for the festival of lamps. Scholars believe the three inks marked income, expenses and loans, though the key to the colours has been lost. A facsimile was printed in the last century, and a digital scan is available to researchers on request.
